mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the success-implies-allowed fact lets Alloy invent a successful customer DecideApp operation, which directly contradicts the permission matrix in the contract.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_LeastPrivilegeViolation { some op: Operation | op.caller.role = CustomerRole and op.kind = DecideApp and op.outcome = Success }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the matrix closed-world fact lets Allowed contain unauthorised cells; the injection then forces a forbidden customer audit-trail grant, which violates FR-021 and the deny side of the matrix.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_PermissionMatrixViolation { CustomerRole -> ViewAudit in PermMatrix.Allowed and ComplianceReviewerRole -> DecideApp in PermMatrix.Allowed }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the no-duplicate-events fact and injecting two audit entries on the same application with the same newStatus directly demonstrates the append-only / one-per-change invariant breaking.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some a: LoanApplication | some disj e1, e2: a.events | e1.newStatus = e2.newStatus and e1.prevStatus = e2.prevStatus }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the journey-match fact lets an Approved application exist without the full chain of audit entries; the injection forces such an under-audited decided application to exist.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditCompletenessViolation { some a: LoanApplication | a.status = Approved and #a.events = 1 }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the customer-views-own constraint and injecting a successful ViewApp by a customer against an application owned by another customer is exactly the breach FR-020 forbids.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OwnershipBasedAccessViolation { some op: Operation | op.caller.role = CustomerRole and op.kind = ViewApp and op.outcome = Success and some op.target and op.target.customer != op.caller }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the no-leakage fact lets the system return PermissionDenied to a customer probing a non-owned reference, revealing existence — exactly what FR-020's 404-not-403 rule forbids.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_NoInformationLeakageViolation { some op: Operation | op.caller.role = CustomerRole and op.kind = ViewApp and some op.target and op.target.customer != op.caller and op.outcome = PermissionDeniedOutcome }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the attribution fact and injecting a decide-event whose actor isn't the assigned officer produces a misattributed audit entry, breaking the FR-017 / attribution-correctness invariant.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AttributionCorrectnessViolation { some a: LoanApplication, e: a.events | e.prevStatus = UnderReview and e.actor != a.assignedOfficer }
